name: Oyster Soup (No. 1)
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Strain the liquor from the oysters, add to it the water, and set it over the fire to heat slowly in a covered vessel
When it is near boiling, season with pepper and salt; add the oysters, and let them stew until they ruffle on the edge, about five minutes
Put in the butter with the milk which has been heated in a separate vessel, and stir well for two minutes
Serve with sliced lemon and oyster or cream crackers

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Strain the liquor from the oysters, add to it the water, and set it over the fire to heat slowly in a covered vessel
2. When it is near boiling, season with pepper and salt; add the oysters, and let them stew until they ruffle on the edge, about five minutes
3. Put in the butter with the milk which has been heated in a separate vessel, and stir well for two minutes
4. Serve with sliced lemon and oyster or cream crackers
